title: Calculus
intro: The mathematics of continuous change: what a quantity is heading towards, how fast it is changing, and how much of it has built up.

blocks.text: Arithmetic and algebra handle things that stay put or change at a steady rate. A car at a constant 20 metres per second covers 100 metres in 5 seconds, and one multiplication gives the answer. Calculus is for the other case, where the rate itself keeps changing: a falling stone speeds up, a capacitor charges quickly at first and then slowly, a signal wiggles.

Two questions come up again and again. First: how fast is this quantity changing right now? That is the derivative. Second: if I know how fast something is changing at every moment, how much has it changed altogether? That is the integral. Both are answered the same way: make an approximation, make it finer, and see what number it is heading towards. That last idea is the limit, so it comes first.

items: Limits (#/math/calculus/limits): what it means for a function to head towards a value, even where it is not defined.
Derivatives (#/math/calculus/derivatives): rates of change and slopes, built from a limit, with the rules for computing them.
Integrals (#/math/calculus/integrals): signed area built from thin rectangles, the fundamental theorem that connects it to derivatives, and integrals that run to infinity.

blocks.text: You should be able to rearrange simple equations, read a graph, and work with powers such as $x^2$. The exponential function $e^x$ and the sine function appear in a few examples.
